title: Bonus $1200 Gift Card with Telstra $99 300GB Per Month 24-Month Plan (New/Port-in Customers, in-Store/ Callback) @ JB Hi-Fi
body:
Deal: Bonus $1200 Gift Card with Telstra $99 300GB Per Month 24-Month Plan (New/Port-in Customers, in-Store/ Callback) @ JB Hi-Fi

[AppleSmack] iPhone Pro Max $2249 - $1200 = $1049 + $99 over 24 months = $3425
[docbargin] Which means a (sort of) 50% discount off an arguably way overpriced product, in JB money so not really true discount. May suit some who can write it off with the Australian Tyrant Organisation.
[AppleSmack] Its only $49 for 4 months, then reverts to $99. So if you use the phone i mention above, going with Telstra is a total of $4474.96 over 24 months.
[CharcoaI] Incorrect. It's $99 per month, every month over 2 years.
$99 plan price x 24 months = $2376 over 2 years
$2376 - $1200 gift card = $1176 (total over 2 years)
$1176 / 24 months = $49 per month.
[AppleSmack] @CharcoaI: Incorrect, have another look at Telstra website, iPhone Pro Max does NOT get the $1200 credit, the $99 plan is only $49 for 4 months, then reverts to premium price afterwards, unless you can show me otherwise?
[Mayjew] @AppleSmack: https://www.jbhifi.com.au/pages/upfront-mobile-plans
JB has seperate plans for Telstra. Still on the same network etc.
[AppleSmack] @Mayjew: Yeah i understand that, but the comment was specifically Premium Telstra Plan, not JB Telstra plan, so i was referring to that plan
[revheadgl] Perhaps I am missing something, but other than absolutely needing that amount of data for work or a tax dodge, these types of plans are way overpriced.
I am now retired, but even if any recent former employer offered me this, I would simply refuse and ask for 12 month $250-sh plan.
[AppleSmack] Whilst i dont disagree, and yes there are cheaper alternatives out there for roughly the same data, but people these days, especially the young ones would probably use a lot more data than a retiree. Im not having a go at retiree's, my father uses probably 15GB a month, his grandson uses about 300GB a month, different lifestyles, different data consumption.
[revheadgl] Fair point. My data usage is quite high when at home. Away, it's just typically some music and basic internet stuff.
[AppleSmack] Even still, its crazy how people go directly to Telstra or Optus (unless there are cracking deals), their pricing is pretty bad, especially when you compare it to other companies who use their network. I think Tangerine has 320GB for $30 for 3 months, but then goes to $60 atm.
[p3r514n] @AppleSmack: I assume it's to get the full uncapped network speed. I'm paying $37.33/m with Optus for 150GB over 36 months which included a $1500 HN gift card that was used towards a PS5 Pro. Made sense for me at the time.
[revheadgl] @p3r514n: I am on an a grandfathered Amaysim 4G phone plan and I am getting 150-160 down and 50-60 up.
My TPG 4G internet plan is capped at 20, lol. I am moving soon so can't be bothered changing it at this point:)
[Big L] I'll probably grab this because Optus was awful for me, and I'm now with superloop whose billing is atrocious and they're a Telstra wholesale provider. If you want the Telstra network, it's Telstra or JB only, and it's the only network I've never had issues with.
[WaveZero] The deals for $2,000+ off Samsung or Honor phones were better, because the $2,000 was issued as a gift card and JB offers a 30-day change-of-mind policy. You could get a refund on the phone while keeping the $2,000 gift card to use on any purchase, which is even better if you use it for a tax-deductible purchase or salary sacrifice. I know a few people who did this and got the iPhone Duo for $2,000 off, and they also get to expense the $99 phone plan as a tax deductible expense.
[jaboday423] A 30-day change-of-mind policy does not automatically mean promotional gift cards can be retained after returning the phone. The promotion's terms may require the gift card to be returned or its value deducted from the refund.
Isn't it?
[mrmaltalian] You’re basically paying for a gift card and spreading that repayment cost out over 24 months. Don’t be fooled
[Big L] You can't get a Telstra (not wholesale) plan for $49 a month.
[Ghadi] Rip to the jb hi fi gift card method 😢 gone but never forgotten
